summary: Design validation PASSED at fork head 2a5127ff30608f7ea0248277df83c5daea4d1927 (re-verified live at filing; clean normal clone; the head adds the busy thread gauge, its docs line, and the strengthened bridge test over the round-3 head). EXACT-HEAD LEGS: bridge test 2/2 at seed 18616; tidy zero changes; root check -x test exit 0; dev build exit 0; tree clean throughout. PACKAGED LEG (dev distribution, Prometheus scrapes): with controlled traffic between baseline and after scrapes, method GET rose exactly +3 (the valid select, the invalid-collection select, and the baseline scrape's own GET, each attributed), method PUT rose exactly +1 (the single outside-context PUT), responses 4xx rose exactly +2 (the invalid-collection GET and that PUT, so the PUT's own 4xx increment is one and only one), and 2xx rose exactly +2. Pool labels all present: current 10, idle 6, busy 4 which equals current minus idle exactly, max 10000, queued 0. The first packaged attempt read no series because /admin/metrics defaults to Prometheus text on this version and the attempt's parser expected JSON; the leg was rerun with the correct format and full accounting, and both attempts' logs are in the evidence. BEHAVIORAL PROBES (scratch clone, test-only patch preserved at 321 lines, production code untouched; final run 4/4 at seed 18616): a held request raises active and is counted by method and response class exactly once, at completion; an unhandled handler failure counts its method and a 5xx and returns active to baseline; four synchronously blocked requests show active +4 with busy 7 and idle 1 during the hold and are each counted exactly once (final GET 5 including the baseline request); busy equals current minus idle in every snapshot. Two probe-side races in earlier attempts (a stale latch shared across test methods and a racy busy-baseline sample) were fixed in the probe and are part of the preserved history; no production counter misbehaved in any run. ASYNC AND ABORT SEMANTICS, recorded as observed: a request held asynchronously releases its pool thread, so busy does not track async-held work while active does; a transport-aborted request in the raw handler chain does not complete by itself (that layer has no async timeout), and when its cycle is closed by failing the callback it is counted once by method and lands in the 5xx class, because the failed completion carries status 500. LIFECYCLE LEGS: with <metrics enabled="false"/> in a scaffolded solr home the packaged node started normally, answered 200 on the system endpoint, returned 'Metrics collection is disabled' from /admin/metrics with zero jetty series, and stopped cleanly (a first attempt with a bare two-file home hung in cloud init for unrelated scaffolding reasons; the control with the same flag in a complete home starts immediately, and both attempts are logged). A stop-and-restart of the enabled node reset the counters (GET total 2 after restart, from this boot's readiness and scrape traffic only) with deltas matching exactly the new boot's requests, no stale callback and no duplicated counts, and a clean stop. An embedded CoreContainer with no servlet layer initialized and shut down cleanly with the solr.jetty reader absent (only solr.node registered), matching the provider's explicit absent-attribute return.
design_assessment: Against SOLR-18616's two named gaps, the design is sufficient. Abnormal-request visibility: requests that never reach a valid collection or core are counted by method and response class at the server handler, including the outside-context case the ticket calls out. Saturation visibility: current, idle, busy, max and queued pool gauges plus the active-request gauge expose pool exhaustion, and busy (current minus idle) is honest arithmetic whose documented caveat (it includes leased and non-request Jetty work) the probes confirm in both directions: synchronously blocked request threads are inside busy, asynchronously held requests are not, and the active gauge is the one that tracks those. Architecturally the bridge keeps counting in a server-classpath Jetty EventsHandler and carries a Supplier snapshot through a servlet-context attribute into Solr's metric manager under its own registry, with the provider owning and closing the registration, and it degrades silently and safely when the attribute is absent or metrics are disabled. Deliberately absent, consistent with the ticket asking for visibility rather than Dropwizard parity: no per-request timing histograms, no decayed rate meters, and no async-specific counters; rates are derivable from the counters at scrape time in the OTel model. No lifecycle or semantic defect requiring an implementation change was observed. Two observations are recorded for the owner's judgment, neither blocking: an aborted request closed by failure is reported in the 5xx class (Jetty's failed-completion status), which a reader could mistake for an application error and which a docs line could preempt; and the production async-abort path itself (servlet-layer timeout closing an aborted Solr async request) was not executed in this gate, so its accounting rests on the handler-layer semantics proven here plus the container's timeout behavior, stated as a scope limit rather than assumed.
